title: Resolve a matrix model of "latest" to the newest model of the row's family
lead: *Proposed.* When a matrix row's model asks for the latest model of a family, ork resolves it to the newest model of that family when it builds the plan, and runs that model. The lineup entry keeps both: the text the matrix gave (`requested`) and the model ork resolved (`model`). The engine, the adapters, the run record and the slicer ledger all get the resolved name. How plans and lineups show it is the next slice, `models-latest-display`.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
Owner, 2026-11-02 (interactive): models are unpinned from version everywhere; the default is the vendor's latest unless the owner asks for a version. The owner chose "latest within a family": ork picks the newest model of the family the row names, not the vendor CLI's default.

Today the model text goes to the CLI unchanged. The matrix `model` is free text (`slicer/src/slicer/roles.py:172-183`). ork copies it into the lineup (`internal/daemon/runs.go:418`, `:437`; spec check `internal/daemon/speccheck.go:116`), the engine copies the entry into the role request (`internal/engine/round.go:306`, `:324`; `internal/engine/speccheck.go:242`), the runners copy `req.Model` into the adapter spec (`internal/daemon/runner.go:40`, `:113`), and the adapters add the flag when the text is not empty (codex `-m MODEL`, `internal/agent/codex/codex.go:63-65`; claude `--model MODEL`, `internal/agent/claude/args.go:39-41`). So a row that says `latest` reaches codex as `-m latest`. The Grok rows r21-r24 say `latest` today (`slicer relay-roles show --root .`, 2026-11-02); ork skips them until S72.

What each vendor CLI offers (read from `--help` only on 2026-11-02; no model call was made and no credential file was read):
- claude 2.1.316: no list command. `--model` takes "an alias for the latest model (e.g. 'fable', 'opus', or 'sonnet') or a model's full name" (`claude --help`). The CLI already resolves a family alias to that family's latest model. The matrix's Claude rows use `opus`, `sonnet` and `haiku`.
- codex-cli 0.166.0: `codex debug models [--bundled]`, "Render the raw model catalog as JSON"; `--bundled` "Skip refresh and dump only the bundled catalog shipped with this binary" (`codex debug models --help`). Not run, so the JSON shape is not known. `-m, --model <MODEL>` on `codex` and `codex exec`.
- grok 1.0.70: `grok models`, "List available models and exit" (`grok models --help`); no `--json` flag in that help. The orchestrator ran it on 2026-11-02 and saw `grok-4.7 (default)`, `grok-4.7-build-fast`, `grok-4.6`, `grok-4.5` and `ollama-local-*` lines. `-m, --model <MODEL>` "Model ID to use".

Design (owner, 2026-11-02, interactive question: all the design points below were accepted as written; the names and syntax stay *proposed* until an adj record decides them):
- How a row names its family: the model text `FAMILY@latest`, where FAMILY is a model name with one `*` standing for the version (digits and dots only), for example `gpt-*-sol@latest` or `grok-*@latest`. A text without `@latest` is a pinned name and is passed unchanged, as today. For claude, a FAMILY that is one of the CLI's aliases (`opus@latest`, `sonnet@latest`, `haiku@latest`) resolves to the alias itself, with no list call: the claude CLI resolves the alias.
- Bare `latest` (the Grok rows today): refused at plan with `model "latest" names no family; write FAMILY@latest, for example grok-*@latest`.
- Resolving: the daemon reads the vendor's list once and keeps it in memory for the daemon's life (a restart reads again): codex through `codex debug models --bundled`, grok through `grok models` (first word of each line). The newest model is the matching name with the highest version, compared number by number (`4.10` > `4.9`). Names that do not match the whole pattern (`grok-4.7-build-fast` against `grok-*`) are ignored.
- When the list cannot be read or nothing matches: the plan is refused with the command, its exit and the family, so the owner sees it before any start and can override that role's lineup at launch.
- Recording: `runrec.LineupEntry` gains `Requested string \`json:"requested,omitempty"\``; `Model` holds the resolved name. A resumed or retried round uses the recorded `Model`, so a run never changes model halfway. The ledger step gets the resolved name.
- Launch overrides: an override model `FAMILY@latest` is resolved the same way; the check at `internal/daemon/runs.go:463-465` (model must not be empty) stays.

Order: until this slice lands and the owner's daemon is rebuilt, ork passes `-m latest` to codex for any row whose model is `latest`; the owner changes the Codex rows (r9, r12, r15) only after that. S72's Grok runner gets the resolved model through the same lineup, so S72 needs no resolver of its own, only a list reader for grok (this slice adds it).

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- `TestParseSpecReadsFamilyAtLatest` (`internal/models`): `gpt-*-sol@latest` gives family `gpt-*-sol`; `opus` and `gpt-6.1-sol` are pinned; `latest`, `@latest`, `a*b*@latest` (two stars) and `gpt-*-sol@newest` are errors. Fails first: no package.
- `TestNewestComparesVersionsNumberByNumber`: from `grok-4.5`, `grok-4.10`, `grok-4.9`, `grok-4.7-build-fast` and `ollama-local-x`, `grok-*` gives `grok-4.10`; no match is an error naming the family.
- `TestListGrokReadsTheFirstWordOfEachLine`: the captured `models.txt` gives the names (the first word after each bullet line; header lines have no bullet), with `(default)` dropped.
- `TestListCodexReadsTheCatalog`: the captured JSON gives the names (the `slug` of each entry of `models`).
- `TestListersRunTheListCommand`: `ListGrok` runs `models` and `ListCodex` runs `debug models --bundled`; a failing list names the command and its exit.
- `TestClaudeAliasResolvesWithoutAListCall`: `opus@latest` gives `opus` and runs nothing.
- `TestResolveUsesTheVendorList`: `Resolve` returns the newest model and the requested text; a failed list or no match names the family.
- `TestRunPlanResolvesLatestWithinAFamily` (`internal/daemon`): a matrix row `gpt-*-sol@latest` with a fake list gives a lineup entry `{Model: "gpt-6.2-sol", Requested: "gpt-*-sol@latest"}`; a pinned row has no `Requested`. Fails first: the entry holds the raw text.
- `TestRunPlanRefusesBareLatest`: a row with model `latest` refuses the plan with the message in Why.
- `TestRunPlanRefusesWhenTheListFails`: the list command exits 1: the plan error names the command and the family; no run starts.
- `TestModelListIsReadOncePerDaemon`: two plans make one list call per vendor.
- `TestResumedRoundKeepsTheRecordedModel`: a stored run whose entry has `Model: "gpt-6.2-sol"` resumes with that model even when the fake list now says `gpt-6.3-sol`.
- `TestLaunchOverrideResolvesLatest`: an override `codex gpt-*-sol@latest medium` is resolved.
- `TestLaunchOverrideRescuesAFailedResolution`: an override of a role replaces its rows before resolution, so a family that cannot be resolved does not refuse the plan.
- `TestLocalMarkStaysWithItsRow`: a Local-vendor row marks only its own entry: an equal cloud entry in another role resolves, and an override of the Local role drops its mark.
- `TestSpecChainResolvesLatestWithinAFamily`: the spec check chain is resolved.
- `TestLineupEntryKeepsRequestedBesideTheResolvedModel` (`internal/runrec`): `requested` round-trips and a pinned entry writes no key.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Captures first (the owner allowed these two runs on 2026-11-02): run `codex debug models --bundled` and `grok models` once each, with the CLIs' own login, no model call, no credential file read; check the output for tokens or account ids before keeping it. If either is refused or fails, stop and report; do not write a parser against a guessed shape.
2. Write the failing tests; see each fail for the reason given.
3. `internal/models`: the parser, the compare, the listers, the alias table. No dependency.
4. Daemon: resolve at plan, in the spec-check chain and in overrides; cache per vendor; refuse as in Why.
5. Docs; CHANGELOG last.
6. Do not touch the adapters, the engine's request building, `internal/tui`, `internal/cli` text, or the matrix.

Local rows (added 2026-11-07). Never resolve the model of a local row; pass its text through as it is. A local row is one whose Agent is a local launcher (`claude-local`, `codex-local`, `grok-local`; adj 188, S301) or whose vendor column is `Local` (matrix row r33, Agent `Local (vLLM)`, model `qwen3.8-27b`; `slicer relay-roles show`, 2026-11-07). Its model names an entry on the local server, not a vendor family, and `codex debug models` and `grok models` list the vendor's cloud catalog (the 2026-11-02 `grok models` output also had `ollama-local-*` lines). The superseded adj 185 selected the local Grok entry with `grok -m studio-local`; under adj 188 the `grok-local` launcher does that itself, and ork passes no `-m studio-local`. So `ParseSpec` is not called for a local row, a local row with `@latest` in its model is refused at plan time with a message that local models are pinned, and the model cache never runs a list command for a `-local` vendor. Tests: `TestRunPlanPassesALocalRowsModelThrough` (a row with Agent `grok-local` and model `qwen3.8-27b`, and a `Local` row with the same model, plan with that text and no `Requested`, and the fake list is never called) and `TestRunPlanRefusesLatestOnALocalRow`.

Owner approved the proposed Grok matrix edits (r21-r24 and r31 to grok-*@latest) on 2026-11-09 in an interactive question (relay session 8d711f67); apply them after S301 lands.
